The *Kumudadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 162) is a Pali biographical verse text preserved in the Therāpadāna division of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. As indicated by its title, the narrative details the spiritual aspiration and merit of the elder (thera) Kumudadāyaka, particularly focusing on his past karmic act of offering a water lily (*kumuda*). SuttaCentral records five translations of the text across five modern languages, without listing a formal English title [SuttaCentral].
No curated external parallels are identified in SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse metrics from DharmaNexus reveal 47 internal Pali text matches across five compositions [DharmaNexus]. By far the most substantial correspondence is with the first volume of the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo), which shares 39 matching passages (spanning §1.1–6.4 to §2577–2588 with a 0.94 similarity score), pointing to extensive citation or preservation of the verses within the commentarial tradition [DharmaNexus]. The text also exhibits recurring formulaic apadāna phrasing shared with other Therāpadāna poems, including the *Pallaṅkadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 152, §6.3–11.1 aligned with §4.4–9.1), the *Isimuggadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 187, §5.2–7.3 aligned with §4.1–6.3), the *Ekacāriyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 191), and the *Muṭṭhipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 107) [DharmaNexus].
